import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_54/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_54/training_1.csv"

# Load Source 0: schema ['ID', 'G1', 'G2', 'G3']
# index_col=0 to ignore the first column as per Hint 24
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Load Source 1: schema includes 'sex' and 'ID' among many other columns
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Transformation plan:
# - Target schema: ['sex': string, 'G1': float, 'G2': float, 'G3': float]
# - Source0 has G1, G2, G3 but no sex column.
# - Source1 has sex but no G1, G2, G3 columns.
# - Both have 'ID' column which can be used as join key.
# - Join Source0 and Source1 on 'ID' to get sex + G1, G2, G3.
# - Select and reorder columns to match target schema.
# - Ensure types: sex as string, G1,G2,G3 as float.

# Join on 'ID' (index after reading with index_col=0)
# Both df0 and df1 have index as ID, so join on index
df_joined = df1[['sex']].join(df0[['G1', 'G2', 'G3']], how='inner')

# Convert types explicitly
df_joined['sex'] = df_joined['sex'].astype(str)
df_joined['G1'] = df_joined['G1'].astype(float)
df_joined['G2'] = df_joined['G2'].astype(float)
df_joined['G3'] = df_joined['G3'].astype(float)

# Reset index to default integer index (optional, but target examples show default index)
df_result = df_joined.reset_index(drop=True)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_54/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_result.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_54/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_54/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'ID' column (primary key)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="ID", how="inner")

# Group by 'sex' and aggregate mean of G1, G2, G3
result = joined.groupby("sex", as_index=False).agg({
    "G1": "mean",
    "G2": "mean",
    "G3": "mean"
})

# Write output with exact target schema and column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_54/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
